title: CALM: Co-evolution of Algorithms and Language Model for Automatic Heuristic Design
claim: Existing LLM-driven heuristic search keeps the model frozen; ours adds reward-driven fine-tuning so the model co-evolves with the search.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, left-to-right flow in each, new components in bright color
description: Two rounded boxes are shown side by side. The left box, titled 'Existing LLM-based AHD Methods' in a black label, shows a loop. A Heuristic Base, holding idea, code and performance icons, feeds an Operator Base through selection. The operators are Crossover, Simplify, Initialize, Mutate and Reflect. Operator outputs go to a frozen, pale-blue LLM. Its idea and code outputs go to an Evaluation Env., and performance returns to the Heuristic Base. The right box, 'Our CALM Framework' in a blue label, repeats this loop. It adds blue and purple elements: diversity-based selection, new Inject and Replace operators, and a flaming learnable LLM. It also adds response analysis, a GRPO fine-tune arrow, and a reward function. A vertical purple gradient ranks outcomes from better algorithm down to no idea. The eye goes to the orange flame LLM.
caption: Pipeline of existing LLM-based AHD methods [ref] under a fixed LLM and our new approach CALM that enables the co-evolution of LLM in the iterative heuristic search process. New components are presented in bright colors.
abstract: Tackling complex optimization problems often relies on expert-designed heuristics, typically crafted through extensive trial and error. Recent advances demonstrate that large language models (LLMs), when integrated into well-designed evolutionary search frameworks, can autonomously discover high-performing heuristics at a fraction of the traditional cost. However, existing approaches predominantly rely on verbal guidance, i.e., manipulating the prompt generation process, to steer the evolution of heuristics, without adapting the underlying LLM. We propose a hybrid framework that combines verbal and numerical guidance, the latter achieved by fine-tuning the LLM via reinforcement learning based on the quality of generated heuristics. This joint optimization allows the LLM to co-evolve with the search process. Our method outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines across various optimization tasks, running locally on a single 24GB GPU using a 7B model with INT4 quantization. It surpasses methods that rely solely on verbal guidance, even when those use significantly more powerful API-based models.
